title: Sum rules and density-wave modes in spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall fluids
authors: Ritajit Kundu, Rakesh K. Dora, Dung Xuan Nguyen, Ajit C. Balram
abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states are prototypical examples of strongly interacting topologically ordered systems. In this work, we obtain thermodynamic fits on the plane for the pair correlation function, and its Fourier transform, the static structure factor, of two-component spin-singlet Halperin and Jain FQH fluids by expanding them in the recently introduced basis of the orthogonal associated Laguerre polynomials [Fulsebakke et al., SciPost Phys. 14, 149 (2023), https://doi.org/10.21468/SciPostPhys.14.6.149 ] and ascertaining the expansion coefficients by fitting them to large-system Monte Carlo data evaluated using their trial wavefunctions. In this fitting procedure, aside from constraining the exact short-distance behavior of the wavefunction, we also derive and enforce the sum rules that the long-wavelength expansion of the static structure factor must adhere to. We show that incorporating these constraints is crucial for obtaining numerically stable and accurate values of the long-wavelength Girvin-MacDonald-Platzman (GMP)/symmetric density-wave excitation gap. We further extend this approach to spin-resolved density-correlation functions, enabling the evaluation of the gap of the antisymmetric density-wave mode for these spin-singlet FQH states. Finally, we use the density-correlators to compute variational energies of the states and construct phase diagrams for bilayer FQH systems. These could be relevant for understanding recent bilayer FQH experiments that map out the phase diagram by tuning the interlayer separation and density-imbalance/layer-polarization.
summary: This work develops a sophisticated theoretical method using Laguerre polynomials and sum rule constraints to analyze spin-singlet Fractional Quantum Hall fluids. By accurately determining the density-wave excitation gaps for both symmetric and antisymmetric modes, the authors provide crucial insights into the phase diagrams of bilayer FQH systems relevant to modern experimental platforms.
main_problem: To accurately calculate long-wavelength density-wave excitation gaps for spin-singlet Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) fluids.
main_result: The authors show that incorporating sum rules derived from the static structure factor expansion is crucial for obtaining numerically stable and accurate values for both symmetric and antisymmetric density-wave excitation gaps.
method: They perform thermodynamic fits on the pair correlation function using an orthogonal basis of associated Laguerre polynomials, enforcing necessary sum rules during the fitting procedure.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-component spin-singlet FQH fluids (Halperin and Jain states) in a strong perpendicular magnetic field. The framework is extended to analyze bilayer FQH systems.
key_observables: Long-wavelength Girvin-MacDonald-Platzman (GMP)/symmetric density-wave excitation gap, antisymmetric density-wave mode gap, and variational energies for phase diagram construction.
important_parameters:
Filling fractions ($
u$), interlayer separation, and density imbalance/layer-polarization in bilayer systems.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes confinement to the Lowest Landau Level (LLL) and relies on expanding correlation functions using an orthogonal polynomial basis.
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework by fitting pair correlation functions using Laguerre polynomials, enforcing sum rules derived from the static structure factor expansion. This is applied to calculate excitation gaps and ultimately construct phase diagrams for bilayer FQH systems.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the rigorous mathematical techniques involving orthogonal polynomial expansions and constraint enforcement (sum rules) are highly relevant to developing robust theoretical tools for strongly interacting quantum many-body systems, which share conceptual links with AMO physics modeling of few-body or lattice excitations.

FIG. 5. Variational phase diagrams of bilayer FQH states. Phase diagrams in the interlayer separation-polarization (d/ℓ, γ) plane for (a) bosons at filling νb=2/3, and fermions at fillings (b) ν=2/5 and (c) ν=2/3 obtained from calculations comparing the per-particle Coulomb energies of the competing candidate states listed on the panels and identifying the state with the lowest energy at each point. Solid lines denote phase boundaries. At non-zero polarizations (γ>0), only the fully polarized (I) and layer-decoupled (III) states compete, whereas at γ=0 the singlet (II) state is also relevant. The hatched area shown below γ=0 highlights the phase diagram on the γ=0 line.
